newsitem.title: FRANCE: French EdF strike Weds, no power cuts expected.
newsitem.headline: French EdF strike Weds, no power cuts expected.

text.p: France's Communist-led CGT union has called a one-day strike for Wednesday at state electricity utility Electricite de France (EdF) but power cuts are not expected, unions and EdF management said on Tuesday.
The CGT union represents about half of EdF staff. It is the only union calling a strike.
"I don't think there will be any impact on electricity (supply)," a CGT union spokesman told Reuters.
Management at the utility said it was too early to provide a detailed outlook on the impact of the strike.

The CGT, which has long been campaigning for protection of jobs and fighting European Union moves to liberalise national electricity markets, is also opposing a draft deal to cut the working week to 32 hours with staff working the shorter week being paid for 35 hours.

The CFDT, CFTC and CGC unions have backed the draft deal and, according to EdF management, that is a sufficient number for the accord to be adopted as long as those who have said they back it go ahead and sign up.
The idea is to allow for more flexible work hours, cut down on overtime, and to allow more recruitment as a result.
But the agreement, once finalised, would be implemented at local level on a voluntary basis.

Separately, EdF is still negotiating its next four-year contract with the government, including the amount of funds that the state utility hands over to the state each year, with the talks with the government expected to come to a head next month.
